events.text: Mist on West Lake. A poet on a painted boat asks anyone passing to finish his couplet.

ok.log: Your line is better than his. He pretends it was his idea, then credits you in the published version.

fail.log: Your line rhymes, and that is all it does.

effects.log: Lotus leaves, rain on the water, and nobody asking you to fight anything.

events.text: The silk mills of Suzhou run day and night. A mill owner is looking for guards after a string of night robberies.

choices.text: Guard the mill for a season

ok.log: On the third night the robbers come. On the third night they stop coming. (35 taels)

fail.log: The robbers are a whole gang. You save half the silk and your life.

effects.log: Silk is not worth dying for. You tell yourself that on the way out of town.

events.text: A canal boatman poles you through Suzhou's water lanes, singing a song about a swordsman who drowned for love.

effects.log: It has forty verses. By the thirtieth you are both crying for no reason.

choices.text: Tip him to sing something happier

effects.log: He sings about a fat official falling into a canal. Much better.

events.text: The tea pickers on the hills above Hangzhou sing as they work. One of them is humming a sword form's rhythm.

choices.text: Ask her where she learned it

effects.log: 'My grandfather,' she says. 'He picked tea and swept a sect's steps.' She hums it again for you.

choices.text: Pick tea with them for a day

effects.log: Your fingers are green, your back aches, and you have never slept so well.

events.text: A retired minister's garden in Suzhou is famous for rocks shaped like mountains. He invites passing martial artists to 'improve' them.

choices.text: Split a rock with your palm

ok.log: Clean in two. The minister names the pieces after you.

fail.log: The rock wins. Your palm is purple for a week.

effects.log: He is delighted. Nobody admires the rocks any more. He gives you tea for an hour.

events.text: Pirates of the Jiangnan waterways board your ferry, and their captain is a girl of about fifteen with an enormous hat.

effects.log: She tips the hat. It is a very good hat.

ok.log: One leap, one hat. Her crew laughs so hard they forget to rob anyone.

fail.log: She dodges and you fall in the river. Her crew laughs even harder.

events.text: Two poets in a Nanjing wine house are about to fight a duel over whose poem was better. Neither can hold a sword.

choices.text: Hold the duel as a poetry contest

effects.log: You judge. Both lose. Both buy you dinner.
They both miss, fall over and become friends. The wine house cheers.

events.text: The plum rains: a month of grey drizzle that gets into your clothes, your bones and your mood.

effects.log: Rain on the roof for a month. Your breathing becomes as steady as it.
Everyone complains. It is the most Jiangnan thing you have ever done.

events.text: A salt merchant's wedding in Yangzhou: three days, a thousand guests and a hired martial artist to 'keep the peace'.

effects.log: Nothing happens, which is exactly what they paid for. (25 taels)
The food alone is worth the trip. You meet a very talkative matchmaker.

events.text: In Jiangnan, people say a tiny sect called White Crane Mountain once had the best swordsmen in the south.

choices.text: Ask an old boatman about it

effects.log: 'The Cranes? They fought the Blood Cult alone, a hundred years ago. There were twelve of them left after.' He spits in the river.

choices.text: Go and look at the mountain

effects.log: A leaky roof, one old master, twelve disciples. You wonder what they were.

events.text: Children are stealing lotus pods from the temple pond, and the monk in charge is chasing them with a broom.

effects.log: They share the pods with you. The monk pretends not to see.
You catch one child. He gives you half a pod as a bribe. You accept.

events.text: The river floods the lower town. Everyone with a boat is rowing people to the temple on the hill.

ok.log: Forty trips. Your hands bleed. Nobody drowns in your street.

fail.log: You capsize twice and save four people anyway.

effects.log: Rice, ginger soup and a lot of hands to hold. The temple is warm because of you.

events.text: A travelling Jiangnan opera performs 'The Butterfly Lovers'. The whole town cries, including the magistrate.

effects.log: You cry too. You tell everyone it was the smoke.

choices.text: Go backstage and meet the actors

effects.log: The actor who plays the scholar is a retired swordsman. He shows you how the stage fights are faked.

events.text: An ink-stone carver sells stones from the riverbed. One of them has a vein that looks like a sword.

effects.log: It is the best ink you have ever ground. Your calligraphy improves, or you think it does.

choices.text: Ask him to teach you carving

effects.log: A week of chipping stone. You make one terrible ink stone and a friend.

events.text: A salt smuggler offers you a cut if you ride on his barge past the salt inspectors tonight.

effects.log: The inspectors are paid to look at the stars. (30 taels)
He shrugs. His barge sinks two weeks later, salt and all.

events.text: A beggar in Hangzhou recites classical poetry for coins, better than any scholar you have met.

effects.log: He writes it on your sleeve with charcoal. You never wash that sleeve.

choices.text: Ask how he fell so far

effects.log: 'I passed the exam,' he says. 'Then I told the truth to a minister.' He laughs.

events.text: Lovers write their names on ribbons and tie them to the Jade Belt Bridge. The bridge is more ribbon than stone.

choices.text: Tie a ribbon with no name

effects.log: For whoever it will be. The wind takes it by morning.
Four thousand and eleven. You lose count twice. It is a very peaceful afternoon.

events.text: Summer in the Jiangnan marshes: mosquitoes the size of sparrows, and heat that makes stone sweat.

effects.log: You smell of smoke for a month. The mosquitoes respect it.
You gain some skill and lose a great deal of blood to insects.

events.text: The river towns race dragon boats for the honour of the county. One crew is a rower short.

ok.log: Your crew wins by a head. You are carried through town on the boat.

fail.log: You row like a hero and your crew comes second. Still a feast.

effects.log: You shout until you have no voice. The winners throw you a rice dumpling.

events.text: A master calligrapher in Suzhou challenges anyone who calls themselves a swordsman: 'The brush is also a blade.'

ok.log: Your strokes are so sharp he laughs and hangs your sheet beside his own.

fail.log: Your characters look like drunk swordsmen. He is very kind about it.

effects.log: He writes the character for sword. You see the whole form in one stroke.
